title: Show what changed in a what's-new popup after an update or rebuild
notes:
Show what changed when the app is reinstalled or updated. Agreed with the user (2026-11-06).

- At build time, bundle a changelog: the merged pull requests on main (git log --first-parent of merge commits: commit, date, PR number, title), newest first, capped (e.g. last 200), as JSON in the build. Works for local rebuild.sh builds and for GitHub release builds alike, since both stamp <version>+<commit>.
- The app stores the build it last showed (userData). On the first launch of a build whose commit differs, a popup lists only the entries newer than the last-shown commit (all of them, capped, when none is known), grouped by date, each PR a link to GitHub; a release build also shows its version heading.
- Keyboard first: arrows and Page keys scroll, Enter on an entry opens its PR in the browser, Escape closes; a key (a row in src/shared/keys/actions.ts) and a help-dialog entry reopen it any time.
- Not shown when nothing changed (same commit), and never on the very first install with no history (just remember the build).
- Which entries to show (from last-shown to current) is a small tested module (workflow-rule-2). Help blurb within BLURB_WORD_LIMIT; docs/app updated.

comments.body: Shipped in #220: a what's-new popup lists the PRs merged since the build last shown (bundled from git log at build time, record in userData), Ctrl+Shift+L reopens it. Release builds need a full-history checkout (fetch-depth: 0).
